title: Ethnic-fusion womenswear cut CAC 41% by trading polished influencers for raw creator-UGC
content: A Bengaluru ethnic-fusion womenswear brand (AOV ₹2,400) was burning ₹14L/month of its ₹35-45L paid budget on macro-influencer collabs (50K-300K followers) on Instagram. By Q3 FY25 the math broke: blended CAC had climbed to ₹1,180, Meta ROAS on influencer-seeded campaigns had slipped to 1.7, and the Reels pulled healthy 4-6% saves but only a 0.8% Reel-to-cart rate. The studio-lit content looked like an ad, so it converted like one. The team killed 80% of the macro deals and built a creator-UGC engine: 60 micro-creators (3K-25K followers) on a ₹3,500 flat + product model, briefed to shoot try-on and unboxing in real homes on phone cameras — no ring lights. The best 12 clips ran as Meta Advantage+ catalogue ads; WhatsApp recovered abandoned carts at ₹22 a conversion. Over 11 weeks blended CAC fell to ₹695 (down 41%), Meta ROAS recovered to 3.4, UGC cart rate hit 2.1%, and cost per creative asset dropped from ₹45,000 to ₹3,500.
lesson: When influencer content looks like a polished ad, the feed and the buyer both treat it like one. Phone-shot creator-UGC converts because it reads as a peer recommendation, not bought media — and it scales at roughly 1/12th the creative cost, so you can test 12 angles for the price of one studio shoot.
